18,00 25,00Lake view Cafe at The Westin truly lives up to its reputation as my favorite spot in the city! The location is absolutely stunning, offering a serene and destressing ambiance that's hard to beat. It's definitely a must-visit for anyone looking for a peaceful escape.
The food is undeniably good, and the staff are absolutely great – always attentive and friendly. However, there's certainly room for improvement when it comes to variety.
To enhance the buffet experience, I strongly recommend adding beverages to the buffet selection. Including options like sparkling water, tea, and coffee would be a fantastic enhancement. Additionally, it would be incredibly helpful to have the menu on the table so guests can browse offerings before heading to the buffet. At the live counters, it's often unclear what's being served, so clearer labeling or descriptions would be a welcome addition.
Overall, despite the minor suggestions for variety and menu presentation, Cafe remains a top choice for its beautiful setting and delicious food. It's truly a place to unwind and enjoy!

featured_reviews.review_text:

I definitely will come back to enjoy a good cup of coffee in that wonderful calm atmosphere.

featured_reviews.name: rosh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our inaugural visit to Lake View Café was, regrettably, underwhelming despite its promising premise.

The buffet boasted an impressively expansive spread, encompassing Southeast Asian, Indian, and continental cuisines, reflecting commendable variety and ambition. However, the execution fell short of expectation, with the offerings lacking any discernible “wow” factor.

A particularly notable drawback was the quality of the chicken across several dishes, which appeared less than fresh and was consistently tough, detracting significantly from the dining experience. Even relatively straightforward preparations, such as the pasta, required multiple iterations before reaching an acceptable standard—an avoidable lapse in a setting of this calibre.

Service, too, proved to be disappointingly pedestrian, falling well below the benchmark set by establishments such as JW Marriott Mumbai and Taj Mahal Palace.

In sum, while the breadth of the spread is undeniably impressive, the inconsistency in execution and lacklustre service rendered the experience far from memorable.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Chettinad Tiffun is one such hidden gem in Powai at a 2 minute walking distance from the main road, serving Authentic South Indian, TamilNadu Cuisine prepared in perfect amount of spices at pocket friendly prices.
Its a very cute and small space with a seating for around 10 to 15 people at once having minimal decent decor. They have enough parking space in the outdoor.
We visited during the evening time and tried following dishes -
Chicken Kothukari Idli - Crisp idli with chicken kheema having bang on flavours cooked to perfection served with 2 chutneys and Sambar. Quantity is worth the price and taste is too good.
Chettinad Special Masala Dosa - Loved this dosa having mouth watering scrumptious taste of south Indian flavours. Extremely delicious.
Butter Podi Idli -  I remember trying this dish at Idlish for the first time and I so loved it that I ordered it again over here. This is one of their signature dishes and is definitely worth trying. Its flavorful and fulfilling.
Muttai Dosai (Egg Dosa) - Tried Egg Dosa for the very first time and liked it. Another try on the menu.
Pineapple Sheera - Has a homely sheera feel with  pineapple flavour.
Kumbakonam degree Coffee - Coffee with a healthy twist of palm Jaggery's sweetness. Perfect refreshment.
Cardamom Masala Tea - Their Tea is outstanding.  I so loved it that I  ordered another cup.Youll literally fall in love with this tea with every sip. Its extremely aromatic and refreshing.
They also serve fresh Coconut Water if you wish to have it along with this delicious food. Also we tried their Rasam as a welcome drink and its spicy, full of flavours worth trying.
The staff is very attentive and kind and helped us ordering their best dishes. Even the owner is super kind and generous. Its definitely a must must visit place in Powai after work, with friends or for quick meets over Chai.
They have outlets in Goregaon east and west and Borivali as well.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Prasad Food Divine, Powai, Mumbai, for dinner with my family after reading several positive reviews and noticing its fine-dining positioning. Unfortunately, our experience did not live up to the expectations.

The food was just average—neither bad nor exceptional. While the menu offers a good variety of options, the taste did not justify the premium pricing. Service was another area of concern; it was noticeably slow throughout our visit.

One surprising disappointment was that cold mineral water bottles were not available when requested, which is quite unexpected for a restaurant that presents itself as a fine-dining establishment.

Another major concern was the ambiance. During our dinner, there were two birthday celebrations with loud recorded songs and significant noise levels. While celebrations are understandable, a fine-dining restaurant is generally expected to provide a calm, comfortable, and relatively private dining atmosphere. The excessive noise disturbed the overall experience and made it difficult to enjoy a relaxed family dinner.

Overall, the ambiance is decent, but considering the food quality, service, noise levels, and pricing, we did not find good value for money. Based on our experience, the restaurant did not meet the expectations associated with a fine-dining destination. Hoping the management addresses these concerns and improves the overall guest experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Just visited Mejwani Maharashtrichi in Powai, Mumbai for lunch and it turned out to be a proper Maharashtrian feast! If you love authentic regional food, this place is definitely worth trying.

Started the meal with Kothimbir Vadi – perfectly crisp on the outside and soft inside, packed with coriander flavor. A classic Maharashtrian snack done right.

Next came the Chicken Pahadi and Kabab. The Chicken Pahadi had a nice smoky flavor with mild spices, while the Kabab was juicy, tender, and grilled beautifully. Great starters to kick off the meal.

For the main course, I tried Valacha Birda and Maswadi. Valacha Birda, a traditional Maharashtrian curry made with field beans, had a rich, earthy taste. Maswadi was unique and flavorful, with its spiced gram flour dumplings soaking up the curry perfectly.

Paired everything with Jawari Bhakri, which tasted fresh and authentic – a perfect match for the curries. Also had Green Salad and Steam Rice on the side to balance the meal.

Ended the lunch on a sweet note with Kharvas, a traditional Maharashtrian dessert made from colostrum milk. It was soft, mildly sweet, and flavored with cardamom – the perfect way to finish the meal.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Sigree Global Grill, one of the most famous buffet places in town and our personal favourite. Visited the outlet after a couple of years and it totally lives up to its reputation with a buffet that’s all about variety, flavour and consistency.

Taking you through what all we had:

STARTERS

We were greeted with a welcome drink, Apple Panna. The starters and live counters set the tone perfectly. The soups were comforting, the chaat counter (Pani Puri, Papri Chaat, Crispy Corn Chaat) was the perfect desi twist and the grill section is where Sigree really shines. Vegetarian options like Paneer Tikka, Malai Kalimirch Broccoli, Chermoula Potatoes and Beet Dumplings are well-marinated and evenly grilled. Non-veg starters are equally strong with Chilli Chicken, Achari Murgh Tikka, Basil Pesto & Lemon Mustard Grilled Fish, Amritsari Prawns and Thai-style Chicken Siu Mai. The prawns were really delicious and so was the fish.

LIVE COUNTER

The live pasta counter and pizzas are great add-ons, which only elevates the experience. Both of them were tasty to eat.

MAIN COURSE

The spread is extensive and comforting. vegetarian dishes like Paneer Achari Do Pyaza, Sarson Da Saag with Makki Roti, Dal Amritsari, Thai Green Curry, Soy Chilli Manchurian, Biryani, noodles and assorted breads are well-balanced and satisfying. On the non-veg side, Murgh Mirch Methi, Herb & Garlic Roast Chicken, Baked Fish Jardiniere and the Mutton Dum Biryani stand out for their depth of flavour.

DESSERTS

A fitting finale right from the Jalebi with Rose Rabri, to their multiple mousse options, the cheesecakes to the chocolate pastries, the ice creams alongside their kulfis, the desserts were the perfect end to a delicious meal.

Sigree Global Grill is a dependable, crowd pleasing buffet that delivers on quantity and quality. Ideal for family outings, celebrations, or when you’re just really hungry and want it all. Highly recommended for buffet lovers.

featured_reviews.review_text: Had a great time at Bayroute Powai! We ordered their hummus plate (Arbe), it was delicious and the bread was out of this world! featured_reviews.name: Prasad K
featured_reviews.review_text:
We tried multiple dishes at Bayroute and overall had a very pleasant experience.
The Machboos Al Kuzu was flavourful and aromatic, with beautifully spiced rice and tender lamb — a very satisfying and hearty dish.

The hummus with chicken shawarma add-on and pita bread was absolutely awesome. The hummus was creamy and rich, the shawarma was well-seasoned, and together with warm pita bread it tasted amazing.

The Kuzu (lamb dish) was cooked well and the meat was tender. It was tasty and comforting, though the flavours were on the milder side and felt a little subtle.

The baklava was a complete show, waiter crushed rose on it and  made it feel special, and it tasted amazing. Rich, flaky, and not overly sweet.

Overall, the place is slightly heavy on the pocket, but the ambience is very good, the location is convenient, and the staff is friendly and helpful, which adds a lot to the experience.
I really liked the place and would visit again.

featured_reviews.name: Mishti Khadye
featured_reviews.review_text:
For a video review check my IG page- itsmishtikhadye.

Im hoping my review along with description gives you an idea about things♥️✨

Bayroute, Powai, is a Middle Eastern dream come true! 🌅 The ambience is a warm mix of indoor & outdoor seating, with hot air balloons 🛫️ setting the perfect Middle Eastern vibe — super cozy and Instagram-worthy! 👌 Staff are friendly & attentive, and the washrooms are spotless.

Food Highlights:
- Fateh Dajaj: Succulent shredded chicken in a creamy garlic sauce with crispy bread — addictive & finger-licking good!
- Kebab Halabi: Soft, fresh bread paired with juicy kebabs — a match made in heaven.
- Lavash Crush Chicken Halabi: A biryani-like delight, mild on spice, with lavash crust (crunchy like papad) adding that wow factor.
- Dijaj Tria: A trio of chicken preparations — perfect for those wanting a taste of variety.

Desserts & Drinks:

- Greek Goddess (drink): Refreshing light berry drink — perfect for a chill vibe.

- Salted Caramel Baklava Sheikh*: My fav! Rich, nutty, and that salted caramel twist on classic baklava — divine. Remeber to share it cz it is heavy!

- Kunafa (live experience): Layers of crunchy pastry, dry fruits, and ice cream — utterly mesmerizing & drool-worthy.

Verdict: Bayroute’s food, ambience, and live kunafa prep make it a must-visit for Middle Eastern food lovers! Hot air balloons, good staff, and clean washrooms — they’ve ticked all the boxes. ⭐️
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:

Regards, Team Bayroute

From the moment we stepped in, Bayroute impressed with its warm lighting, elegant interiors, and relaxed yet refined vibe — perfect for date nights or a chill evening with friends.

The grilled kebabs were juicy and fragrant, perfectly seasoned and cooked just right. The shakshuka was rich and comforting, and the saffron rice was a great companion to every dish.

Pairing the food with their mocktails/cocktails elevated the experience — refreshing with the right amount of creativity.

Attentive and friendly staff who were happy to recommend dishes and explain flavours. The pacing between courses was spot-on.

💸 Value:
Pricing is on the premium side, but worth it for the quality, portions, and overall experience.

✨ Overall:
A delightful Middle Eastern escape in the heart of Powai. Food, ambience, and service all deliver — Bayroute is now a must-visit on the Mumbai dining map!

I would happily come back again and would highly recommend this place to anyone who enjoys a good South Indian vegetarian meal.

One of the worst dining experiences I have ever had in Mumbai.
The place is extremely unhygienic, and the overall environment is very poor. The entrance itself was shocking – leaking garbage bins right outside with a horrible stench. The kitchen and surrounding area looked very badly maintained, making it completely unfit for food preparation.
The food quality is terrible. We ordered Beef Roast and Chicken Curry, and both were of extremely poor quality. The beef especially was almost inedible. To make things worse, the photos shown on Google are misleading – they do not belong to this restaurant at all but are taken from somewhere else.
Another shocking fact is that with the same kitchen/location, they have listed multiple restaurants online under different names, which is highly deceptive.
Overall, this was an utterly disappointing and unhealthy experience. Definitely not recommended to anyone.

featured_reviews.name: Pradeep G
featured_reviews.review_text:
My experience with this hotel was very disappointing.
I ordered breakfast, but they delivered a completely different item instead of what I had ordered. When I called to inform them about the mistake, they told me that the ordered item was not available, so they sent a different one without informing me. I was surprised — how can they decide on their own what a customer should eat?
After some discussion, they agreed to replace the item within 30 minutes. However, there was no response afterward. I called five times, but they did not answer the calls, and we never received the replacement.
I then contacted the owner, who assured me that he would check and confirm. He also promised a refund if the item was unavailable. I followed up with him three times regarding the refund, but there was no response.
I have been a regular customer for the past five years and never expected such behaviour from them. After multiple failed follow-ups, I decided to consider the amount as a “donation” for their so-called excellent service.
There are other good Kerala hotels near Powai — I would recommend trying those instead. Based on my recent experience, I would not suggest choosing MTK.

I just wish they had better seating so more people can enjoy their food.

featured_reviews.review_text: I ordered Kerala Chicken and Kerala Porotta. The parotta was completely uncooked, and the quality of the chicken curry was poor. Although I've had the best Kerala chicken curry at this place before, the taste, food quality, and packaging seem to be deteriorating day by day. It's not just the parotta and chicken curry; even the packaging of biryani is excellent before, but now the packaging, quality and taste are not up to par. Furthermore, the late delivery results in us eating cold food. I've been facing this issue in my recent orders, and this time I decided to write a review, hoping that they improve the food quality and bring back the old taste. featured_reviews.name: Uttam Bhat
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a South Indian living in Andheri East, I’m always on the lookout for places that serve authentic South Indian breakfast. While the sheer number of Udupi-style restaurants in the area are okay—or kaam chalau, as we say in Mumbai—none of them really compare to the food back home.
Neyyi is a very welcome change.
The Davangere benne dose hit the right spot—perfectly crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. The potato bhaji served alongside was creamy, well-balanced, and complemented the dosa beautifully. The podi thatte idli was soft and fluffy, with just the right amount of spice in the podi—flavourful without being overpowering, making it enjoyable for all spice tolerance levels.
The real surprise, though, was the cold filter coffee. While I initially considered the idea of cold filter coffee borderline blasphemous, it absolutely works. In fact, I’d happily take this over any cold latte or frappuccino. I’d go so far as to say I’d visit Neyyi just for their cold filter coffee alone.
I’m genuinely glad I stumbled upon this place. For people in Andheri East and Powai, this is the destination for South Indian breakfast cravings—no need to look elsewhere.

featured_reviews.review_text:
‘Khau’ in Marathi translates to eating, and ‘Galli’ means a lane. There are over 10 Khau Gallis in Mumbai, each is known as the treasure trove of street food in the city. One such street is the Ghatkopar Khau Galli which is popular for its heavenly vegetarian street fare. Recently, we got a chance to prowl this galli and discover a paradise of enticing street food joints, restaurants and stalls. Our bucket list features the best things to try at Ghatkopar Khau Galli.

Directions To Ghatkopar Khau Galli

Ghatkopar Khau Galli is located at a half a kilometre’s distance from Ghatkopar Railway Station (East). Thus, catch a local train or metro to Ghatkopar Railway Station, and then take an auto to Ghatkopar Khau Galli.

Ghatkopar Khau Galli Opening Hours

Business at Ghatkopar Khau Galli commences at around noon and runs until midnight. However, some of the stalls don’t start selling food until 2 pm as preparation takes time.

Variety of dishes with quality of yummy and spicy taste. While loitering around the Ghatkopar Khau Galli, if you come across a restaurant that is preparing 10 dosas at a time, on 10 different tawas, know that you’ve reached Sai Swad Dosa. This eatery is so popular that on weekends you might have to wait for over 40 minutes to get your order. The remarkable factor about this dosa joint is that they do not ever compromise on the hygiene and quality of the dishes. The cooks here always use requisite equipment and only the freshest ingredients. They serve 45 different varieties of dosa, the most popular one being the Gini Dosa, which is slathered with Szechuan sauce and is dripping with melting cheese.

What to have: Gini Dosa, Pasta Dosa, Maggi Dosa, Cheese Chocolate Dosa

Perfect for: Evening Snacks
